criteria.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` includes a test where a new-class answer whose normalised name equals an existing live class reuses that class id and adds no registry record.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 28 passed, including introspect::tests::a_new_class_answer_naming_a_live_class_reuses_it. That test writes a live class named "the REVIEWER is not told!" and then applies a new-class answer that differs only in case and punctuation. apply_answer returns None (no class to write), failure_class is the existing id, new_class is false and the status is Recorded. Two controls create a new class: a name that differs by one word, and a name that is empty after normalising. A sibling test covers a retired class's name, which resolves to the live target. The end-to-end test a_new_class_named_like_a_live_class_reuses_it (athena-cli introspection) also passed. Per its plan it checks that the registry holds 1 class after two events. In the code (introspect.rs ~1578-1656), `reused` comes from class_named, and the FailureClass is minted only when `reused` is None.

summary: The change does what was asked: new failure classes are now deduplicated when created, and classes can be merged. One rule, `class_named`, applies at both places a class is created (introspection and `review --new-class`): a new class whose name matches an existing class after normalising reuses that class and writes no new record. A merge is a new append-only record (`ClassStatus::Merged`). Every class reader resolves merged ids in memory, so a merged class's cases count under its target, and the existing records are not touched. I ran the targeted tests and they all pass: `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` (28), `cargo test -p athena-core merge`, `cargo test -p athena-data` (191), and the CLI introspection and review tests (43). The docs and decision D166 are accurate, and the 158 count matches the evidence snapshot. The verdict is still fail, on criterion 4 only: the workspace `cargo test` is red. Six tests in `xtask --test spec` fail because the BRIEF.md addenda dated 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-08 have no requirement in docs/spec.toml. This change doesn't touch either file, so the failure predates it and needs its own job. Minor points: five changed files are outside the expected deliverables list but were in the accepted plan and are justified; the merged record has its own round-trip test instead of being added to the existing one; and no CLI command can trigger a merge yet, which the docs mark as design.
